evidence.quote:
To disable all server-side execution of JavaScript for [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) or [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), you can either:

- Pass the `--noscripting` option on the command line.
- Set [`security.javascriptEnabled`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-security.javascriptEnabled) to false in the configuration file.

If your application does not use server-side JavaScript — $where, $function, $accumulator, mapReduce, or stored system.js functions — you can disable server-side JavaScript on the server, removing the attack surface entirely until you patch.

statements.statement: If the application does not require $where, $function, $accumulator, or mapReduce, disable server-side scripting on mongod and mongos using security.javascriptEnabled: false or --noscripting.
statements.note: Documented in core server-side JavaScript manual options and security advisories.

queries: mongodb disable server-side javascript noscripting security.javascriptEnabled

statements.statement: Inventory application queries before disabling because dependent operations will fail.
statements.note: Advisories advise checking if workloads use server-side functions before turning off scripting to avoid breaking operations.

mongodb disable server-side javascript noscripting security.javascriptEnabled
percona cve-2026-11933 disable server side javascript

edits.rationale: MongoDB documentation confirms that server-side JavaScript execution on mongod and mongos can be disabled via --noscripting or setting security.javascriptEnabled: false. Security advisories recommend auditing query workloads and disabling scripting when not required to eliminate attack surfaces.

edits.old: Percona's June 17, 2026 advisory describes CVE-2026-11933 in the older BSON-to-JavaScript-array conversion path: an authenticated user with read privileges and scripting enabled could trigger memory disclosure or a crash. Its upstream ticket concerns BSON wrapper ownership. This historical evidence does not establish that MongoDB 9.0's WASM engine has the same vulnerability. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-17)

(medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-17) Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/security-advisory-cve-2026-9740-and-cve-2026-11933-in-percona-server-for-mongodb/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/rest/api/2/issue/SERVER-128125

evidence.quote: The vulnerable code path is inside MongoDB Server’s server-side JavaScript engine, specifically in the BSON-to-array conversion routine. When a BSON document is materialized as a JavaScript array for use inside a server-side script, the engine can reach a state where it accesses memory that has already been freed.

CVSS 8.8. High severity. Two demonstrated outcomes:

Information disclosure (reading other content out of the mongod process memory) and

Denial of Service (crashing it).

Upstream tracking: SERVER-128125.

bsonObjToArray and bsonGetImmutable are sibling functions in the MozJS BSON binding layer. bsonGetImmutable ensures the BSONObj it works with is owned before creating JS wrappers around it;  bsonObjToArray does not apply the same treatment.

evidence.quote: Starting in MongoDB 8.0, server-side JavaScript functions ($accumulator, $function, $where) are deprecated. MongoDB logs a warning when you run these functions.

MongoDB 9.0 re-enables these functions using a WebAssembly (WASM)-based JavaScript engine, which improves security through stronger sandboxing and isolation than prior versions. These functions were previously deprecated in MongoDB 8.0.
